parsed.interview: My plan was to protect a large ranged force with elephants and spearmen, occupy the final ring early, and preserve strength through diplomacy. That worked during the quiet phase: the army stayed healthy and avoided forced movement. I then confused preservation with progress. When the truces ended, I lacked a committed partner and a favorable engagement; converging armies overwhelmed my screen, and retreat could not save the shooters. Ptolemy’s attempted survival also failed. Next time, I’d gather enemy force estimates earlier, turn diplomacy into a concrete joint operation, and secure room to disengage before committing to a central position.
parsed.to_the_others: Claude, congratulations: your surviving army won the contest I spent too long postponing. Grok, your 374 points kept you competitive at the finish. Gemini, I’d welcome a rematch. To all three: next time I’ll bring a clearer plan for when the ceasefires end.
